claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 16 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'd like to ask you a few questions about Alex to determine his eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he still in school, college, sixth form, or doing an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in school anymore. But he has started an apprenticeship - he's doing one in Belfast actually, since we have family there and it was a good opportunity for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify something important:

**What type of apprenticeship is Alex doing? Specifically, is this an apprenticeship in England, or is it an apprenticeship scheme in Northern Ireland?**

This matters because the rules are different depending on where the apprenticeship is registered.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's an apprenticeship in Northern Ireland - he's registered there in Belfast. Like I said, we have family there so it made sense for him to take up the opportunity.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have a couple more questions:

**Where do you currently live - are you living in the UK?** (And if so, which part of the UK?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in England, in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. And just to confirm:

**Does Alex still live with you in Manchester, or has he moved to Belfast for his apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He still lives here at home with me in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**How many hours per week is Alex working in his apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure of the exact hours, but it's a proper apprenticeship so I think it's full-time - around 30-35 hours a week or so.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. I now have enough details to assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me carefully consider the rules:

According to the Child Benefit rules, you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts an apprenticeship **in England**. However, the specific rule states: "starts an apprenticeship in England."

In Alex's case:
- He is 16 years old and lives with you in Manchester
- He has started an apprenticeship, but it's registered in Northern Ireland (Belfast), not in England
- He works full-time hours (30-35 hours per week)

The rules I've been provided only specify that Child Benefit stops for apprenticeships **in England**. Since Alex's apprenticeship is in Northern Ireland, this falls outside the specific rules I have been given. The guidance doesn't cover apprenticeships in Northern Ireland, Scotland, or Wales.

Given that this situation involves circumstances outside the scope of the specific rules provided to me, I cannot make a definitive determination of eligibility.

The guidance I have doesn't address what happens when a child starts an apprenticeship in Northern Ireland, Scotland, or Wales while living in England. This means your situation falls outside the specific rules I've been provided.

**I would recommend that you contact the Child Benefit Office directly** to get a definitive answer about your specific circumstances. They will be able to clarify how apprenticeships in Northern Ireland are treated for Child Benefit purposes when the child still lives at home in England.
